task.name: Internal migration — remove duplicated phase transport config
task.story_text:
## Summary

After the loader bridge (#750) is stable, migrate coordinator internals away from phase-specific duplicated transport fields where it is actually worth doing. This is the internal cleanup that follows the public schema reset.

Part of epic: Config simplification (#264). Story 4 of 5. Depends on #750 (loader bridge).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `PlanConfig`, `PlanAgentReviewConfig`, and `ApiFallbackConfig` no longer carry their own `cli`/`provider`/`model`/`budget_usd`/`timeout` fields — they compose `ModelRef` or reference `ModelProfile` directly.
2. Any config field that exists in types but is not parsed by the loader is either wired up or removed (e.g., `PlanConfig.validate_spec`, `RetryPolicy.plan_escalation_threshold`).
3. `NotificationConfig.human_review_timeout_seconds` default (600) matches the loader default — no silent mismatch.
4. Coordinator phase modules updated to use the composed types.
5. All existing tests pass with the new internal types.

## Notes

- This can land as a fast-follow after v0.8.0 ships (e.g., v0.8.1) if the public schema reset + dogfooding are the release gate.
- The blast radius is internal — no user-facing config changes.
- Guided by existing tests; this is refactoring, not behavioral change.

handoff.summary: Migrated PlanConfig and PlanAgentReviewConfig from duplicated transport scalars to a composed ModelRef, with read-only property views preserving the existing read surface across the coordinator, CLI and sprint runner. ModelRef moved from schema.py to types.py (schema.py re-exports) to resolve the schema-to-types import cycle the composition would otherwise create; a single model_ref_to_profile() helper in bridge.py replaced five hand-rolled ModelRef/PlanConfig to ModelProfile projections in load.py, profiles.py, check_config.py, preflight.py and plan_flow.py. Loaders (_loaders.py, load.py) build the composed types through new PlanConfig.of()/PlanAgentReviewConfig.of() factories that fold the flat forge.yaml keys into a ref. The loader-coverage audit fixed three gaps: the NotificationConfig HITL timeout default (600 typed vs 14400 loaded, now one shared DEFAULT_HITL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS constant), RetryPolicy.plan_escalation_threshold (used in plan_flow control flow but never parsed, now wired up and documented), and the dead EmailConfig stub (removed). Added tests/test_config_composed_phase_refs.py covering type shape, loader normalization, timeout default parity, and a coordinator seam test asserting the profile PLAN actually dispatches is projected from config.plan.ref.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: PlanConfig, PlanAgentReviewConfig, and ApiFallbackConfig no longer carry their own cli/provider/model/budget_usd/timeout fields — they compose ModelRef or reference ModelProfile directly.
acceptance_criteria.notes: PlanConfig and PlanAgentReviewConfig now hold only phase-specific fields (enabled, validate_spec, pool, min_reviewers) plus a composed ModelRef; the old scalars are read-only properties over ref. Asserted structurally in TestComposedShape. No class named ApiFallbackConfig exists — the closest analog is TransportFallbackConfig, which is deliberately unchanged: ModelRef contains a TransportFallbackConfig (api_fallback), so composing the other direction is definitionally circular and would also reintroduce the types-to-schema import cycle. It carries no cli and no budget_usd; its provider/model/timeout_seconds ARE the transport atom, not a duplicated phase config. Documented in the type docstring and asserted in test_transport_fallback_is_the_leaf_atom_a_ref_contains.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Any config field that exists in types but is not parsed by the loader is either wired up or removed (e.g., PlanConfig.validate_spec, RetryPolicy.plan_escalation_threshold).
acceptance_criteria.notes: Audited every dataclass field in types.py against the whole config package. PlanConfig.validate_spec was already parsed. Three genuine gaps found and fixed: RetryPolicy.plan_escalation_threshold (read at plan_flow.py:1604 but never parsed, so unreachable from forge.yaml — wired into the retry parser and documented in docs/guides/inputs-reference.md), NotificationConfig.email/EmailConfig (never parsed, never read — removed), and the notification timeout mismatch covered by AC3. ModelProfile.sandbox_capability_profile is stamped by the coordinator (dev_phase.py:1109) rather than the loader, which is its documented design, so it was left alone.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: NotificationConfig.human_review_timeout_seconds default (600) matches the loader default — no silent mismatch.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Reconciled toward the loader's 14400, not the typed 600. The loader value is what live HITL gates actually use (remote_gates.py, pending_hitl.py); moving the loader down to 600 would have cut real gate windows from 4h to 10min. Both sites now read one DEFAULT_HITL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS constant in types.py so they cannot drift again, with a parity test asserting the typed default and an unconfigured load agree.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Coordinator phase modules updated to use the composed types.
acceptance_criteria.notes: plan_flow.py builds the PLAN dispatch profile via model_ref_to_profile(config.plan.ref, ...); preflight.py uses it for the explicit-planner projection and writes budget scaling through the ref for both plan and plan_agent_review; check_config.py and config/profiles.py migrated to the same helper. Covered by a seam test that runs a full task and asserts the profile PLAN dispatches carries the ref's identity, transport, budget and complexity-scaled timeout.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All existing tests pass with the new internal types.
acceptance_criteria.notes: 7170 passed, 38 skipped. 17 failures remain in test_cut_rc_isolation.py, test_sprint_lock.py and test_sprint_reexec_collision.py — all PermissionError from multiprocessing/synchronize.py (POSIX semaphore creation blocked in the dev sandbox). None of those files reference config code, and they fail identically on the unmodified tree; verified by running them in isolation. Expected to pass under the coordinator's gate, which runs outside this sandbox. Test construction sites were migrated to the new PlanConfig.of()/PlanAgentReviewConfig.of() factories across 41 files — a sanctioned contract-change update, mechanical and assertion-preserving.

story_deviations: Kept the legacy flat scalars as read-only properties rather than deleting them outright. AC1 is about duplicated storage, and delegating accessors leave exactly one source of truth while avoiding a mechanical rewrite of ~60 read sites across the coordinator, CLI and sprint runner. The plan reviewer's note that config/profiles.py's .profiles property must be preserved over the composed fields points the same direction.

Added PlanConfig.of() / PlanAgentReviewConfig.of() factories. These are genuine production API — forge.yaml declares planning transport as flat keys and the loader is their primary caller — not test-only compat shims; they are the one place the flat spelling folds into a ModelRef, mirroring how _normalize_transport folds cli/provider into a TransportSpec.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's file list (load.py, bridge.py, role_derivation.py, secrets.py) omits src/theforge/config/_loaders.py, which is where PlanAgentReviewConfig is actually constructed with the scalar kwargs being removed (_loaders.py:187-195 passes cli=, provider=, model=, budget_usd=, timeout=). Removing those fields breaks that call immediately.
  Suggestion: Add src/theforge/config/_loaders.py to Step 2. Also note the non-construction consumers of the legacy scalars' derived surface: cli/providers.py:45-46, config/profiles.py:80-82, coordinator/audit.py:167 all go through the .profiles property, so they stay stable only if that property is preserved over the composed fields.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 proposes applying 'the same composed representation' to TransportFallbackConfig, but that type is embedded as api_fallback inside both ModelRef (schema.py:53) and ModelProfile (types.py:365), and schema.py imports it from types.py at module scope — making it compose ModelRef would create mutual composition plus a types↔schema import cycle. It also already lacks cli/budget_usd (it carries only provider/model/timeout_seconds + runtime knobs).
  Suggestion: Treat TransportFallbackConfig as already satisfying AC1's intent (it is the minimal transport atom, not a duplicated phase config) unless the audit shows otherwise; if it is restructured, resolve the cycle with a TYPE_CHECKING/lazy import as schema.py already does for TransportSpec.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] AC3 says the 600 default should match the loader, but the loader default is 14400 (secrets.py:57, matching PlanReviewConfig.timeout_seconds); reconciling in the wrong direction would cut live HITL gate windows from 4h to 10min at remote_gates.py:40/183 and pending_hitl.py:42/123.
  Suggestion: Plan already says 'align with the loader default' — make it explicit that types.py:284 moves to 14400 and secrets.py is unchanged.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 names only tests/. The scalar fields are asserted across at least test_config_load.py, test_config_role_derivation_complexity.py, test_complexity_timeouts.py, and test_config_auto_api_fallback.py.
  Suggestion: Enumerate those files so the dev agent does not stop at the first failing suite.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The CLI shared module directly replaces legacy transport fields on the PlanConfig instance (src/theforge/cli/shared.py:485-489). All internal config consumers must be updated to access or mutate transport settings through the new composed ModelProfile or ModelRef structures. Suggestion: Update the CLI shared module to mutate the nested ModelProfile inside PlanConfig instead of direct fields.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The apply_model_info function overloads for PlanConfig and directly replaces legacy transport fields on it (src/theforge/config/models.py:900-926). Model identity and transport mutation helpers must operate on the new composed structures rather than legacy direct fields. Suggestion: Update apply_model_info to delegate to the nested ModelProfile inside PlanConfig.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The CLI runner directly accesses legacy transport fields on the TransportFallbackConfig instance (src/theforge/runners/cli.py:230-257). All runtime dispatch and fallback logic must read transport settings from the composed ModelProfile or ModelRef structures. Suggestion: Update _build_api_fallback_profile to read fields from the nested ModelProfile inside TransportFallbackConfig.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 2 names src/theforge/config/load.py, bridge.py, role_derivation.py, and secrets.py, but PlanAgentReviewConfig is actually parsed in src/theforge/config/_loaders.py::_parse_plan_agent_review and mixed-shape validation lives in _validate_v0_8_schema. If Step 1 removes the legacy scalar fields from PlanAgentReviewConfig without updating _loaders.py, load_config() will still construct the old shape and the new type contract will not load correctly.
  Suggestion: Add src/theforge/config/_loaders.py to the loader migration step and explicitly migrate _parse_plan_agent_review plus the v0.8 schema guard logic to the new composed representation.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 3's caller list misses src/theforge/config/profiles.py::iter_plan_phase_profiles, which currently projects config.plan.cli/provider/model/budget_usd/timeout into a ModelProfile. That function is used by production config/auth inspection paths, so removing those scalar fields from PlanConfig without migrating this caller will break runtime profile iteration outside the listed files.
  Suggestion: Expand the consumer-migration step to include src/theforge/config/profiles.py and any other production helpers that project PLAN/PLAN_REVIEW config into ModelProfile objects.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Refactor the internal coordinator config types to route phase transport settings through the existing composed model/profile abstractions, then migrate consumers in config normalization and coordinator phase code together. Keep the public schema unchanged and treat the missing ApiFallbackConfig name as the likely existing TransportFallbackConfig unless code inspection proves otherwise.

steps.description: Update internal config types to remove duplicated transport fields from planning and fallback configs.
steps.details: Change PlanConfig and PlanAgentReviewConfig so cli/provider/model/budget_usd/timeout are represented by ModelRef or an existing ModelProfile reference instead of duplicated scalar fields. Audit the fallback config named in code, likely TransportFallbackConfig, and apply the same composed representation for provider/model/timeout-style transport settings.

steps.description: Update config loading, bridge, and role derivation to populate the new composed fields.
steps.details: Preserve current public config behavior while constructing the new internal types. Ensure every remaining type field is either parsed from loader input or removed, including a focused audit around PlanConfig.validate_spec and RetryPolicy.plan_escalation_threshold. Align NotificationConfig.human_review_timeout_seconds default with the loader default so typed defaults and loaded defaults cannot diverge silently.

steps.description: Migrate coordinator and CLI consumers from direct duplicated fields to composed transport/profile access.
steps.details: Replace direct reads of phase-specific cli/provider/model/budget_usd/timeout fields with the new composed config access. Keep coordinator control flow and audit-visible values behaviorally equivalent.

steps.description: Update tests around config loading and coordinator phase boundaries.
steps.details: Adjust existing tests for the new internal type shape, add focused coverage for loader-to-type normalization, notification timeout default parity, fallback transport config migration, and coordinator phase access across the touched boundaries.

criteria_mapping.criterion: PlanConfig, PlanAgentReviewConfig, and ApiFallbackConfig no longer carry their own cli/provider/model/budget_usd/timeout fields — they compose ModelRef or reference ModelProfile directly.
Any config field that exists in types but is not parsed by the loader is either wired up or removed (e.g., PlanConfig.validate_spec, RetryPolicy.plan_escalation_threshold).
NotificationConfig.human_review_timeout_seconds default (600) matches the loader default — no silent mismatch.
Coordinator phase modules updated to use the composed types.
All existing tests pass with the new internal types.

risks.description: The spec names ApiFallbackConfig, but preflight found no class by that name.
risks.mitigation: Treat TransportFallbackConfig as the intended target only after confirming the current code has no ApiFallbackConfig equivalent; document the mapping in the implementation notes or test names.

risks.description: The default mismatch direction is ambiguous because the AC says typed default 600 should match loader default, while preflight reports the loader currently defaults to 14400.
risks.mitigation: Choose the existing intended product behavior from nearby tests or config docs, then make both defaults match that value with regression coverage.

risks.description: Changing foundational config types can break indirect consumers outside the obvious coordinator files.
risks.mitigation: Use repository-wide references and the full existing test suite to catch stale direct field reads, but keep migration scoped to internal config normalization and coordinator consumers.
